properties.description: The Cock Tavern. Designed by Hill & Fletcher Architects and erected in 1880. The Coach house and stables were added in 1888. A tavern is first mentioned on this site in 1747

properties.title: The first gay rights demonstration took place here, in Highbury Fields, on 27th
properties.description: The first gay rights demonstration took place here, in Highbury Fields, on 27th November 1970 when 150 members of the Gay Liberation Front held a torchlight rally against police harassment.

properties.title: The Nag's Head
properties.description: The Nag's Head. Locally Listed building. Erected in 1857 by Francis Wragg as a replacement for the original village inn which stood on the corner of Orford Road/Church End. Wragg ran the local stagecoach service to London and also built the adjacent coach houses for his use

properties.title: The Old Schools
properties.description: The Old Schools. This is the original building at Harrow, finished in 1615 and enlarged in 1820 by Charles Robert Cockerell and given its present distinctive appearance.

properties.title: The Old Vicarage
properties.description: The Old Vicarage. Locally Listed building. Erected in 1883 to designs by Habershon & Fawckner as the original Vicarage to St Stephen’s Church which stood nearby. It was converted to a Registry Office in 1924

properties.title: The Princess Of Wales
properties.description: The Princess Of Wales. Blackheath F. C. the oldest open club in the world playing Rugby Union founded 1858 was based here and played on the heath for many years.

properties.title: The round stone in the roadway opposite this point marks the spot where, on
properties.description: The round stone in the roadway opposite this point marks the spot where, on Wednesday the 13th October 1915, at 9.25 p.m. a bomb from a German zeppelin struck the ground and exploded, shattering the chapel windows and doing other material damage.

properties.title: The Surrey Iron Railway
properties.description: The Surrey Iron Railway. Opened in 1803, ran from Wandsworth to West Croydon, and had a branch from Mitcham that terminated in this Borough in 1804. It was the first public railway in the world, was horse-drawn, carried only freight, and operated until 1816. The stone sleepers and rails are original.

properties.title: The Tottenham Outrage

properties.title: Thomas Rainsborough was buried in this churchyard on the 14th November 1648
properties.description: Thomas Rainsborough was buried in this churchyard on the 14th November 1648 after a funeral procession organised by the Leveller movement. Rainsborough was a spokesman for the Levellers and a colonel in the New Model Army. He was killed by a Royalist raiding party during the siege of Pontefract. On the day of the funeral a Leveller leaflet recorded the inscription of Rainsborough's tomb. It proclaimed Rainsborough had made 'King, Lords, Commons, Judges shake, Cities and Committees quake'. He was, it said, 'just, valiant and true'. It ended with the words that here Rainsborough 'bids the noble Levellers adieu'. This plaque was unveiled by Cllr Rania Khan, writer John Rees and politician Tony Benn in 2013.

properties.title: Sewer ventilation lamp
properties.description: Last remaining Victorian sewer gas destructor lamp in London on Carting Lane. Invented to burn methane from sewers to provide light and ventilate the system. A rare historic relic of Victorian engineering, restored and protected.

tags.alt_name: Sewer gas destructor lamp;fart lamp;carting lane lamp;farting lane lamp;James Webb patent sewer gas lamp;Sir Joseph Bazalgette lamp;London's methane sewer gas lamp
tags.description: Last remaining Victorian sewer gas destructor lamp in London on Carting Lane. Invented to burn methane from sewers to provide light and ventilate the system. A rare historic relic of Victorian engineering, restored and protected.
tags.description:de: Letzte viktorianische Abgas-Zerstörerlaterne Londons in der Carting Lane. Erfunden, um Methan aus Abwässern zu verbrennen, Licht zu spenden und das System zu belüften. Seltenes historisches Relikt viktorianischer Technik, restauriert und geschützt.
tags.description:en: Last remaining Victorian sewer gas destructor lamp in London on Carting Lane. Invented to burn methane from sewers to provide light and ventilate the system. A rare historic relic of Victorian engineering, restored and protected.
tags.description:fr: Dernière lampe destructrice de gaz d'égout victorienne à Londres, à Carting Lane. Inventée pour brûler le méthane des égouts, fournir lumière et ventiler le système. Une rare relique historique d'ingénierie victorienne, restaurée et protégée.
tags.description:ja: ロンドンのカーティング・レーンにある最後のビクトリア時代の下水ガス破壊灯。下水からのメタンを燃焼させて光を供給し、システムを換気するために発明されました。ビクトリア朝工学の希少な歴史的遺物であり、修復および保護されています。
tags.description:ko: 런던 카팅 레인에 있는 마지막 남은 빅토리아 시대 하수구 가스 소멸등. 하수구의 메탄을 태워 빛을 제공하고 시스템을 환기하기 위해 발명됨. 빅토리아 시대 공학의 희귀한 역사 유물로 복원되어 보호받고 있음.
tags.description:zh: 伦敦卡廷巷上最后一盏维多利亚时代的下水道气体销毁灯。发明用于燃烧下水道中的甲烷以提供照明和通风系统。维多利亚时代工程的罕见历史遗物，已修复并受保护。
tags.name: Sewer ventilation lamp
tags.note: https://historic-uk.com/HistoryMagazine/DestinationsUK/Farting-Lane
